pinev: Lexington Twp (T111N R24W) centre, from BLM PLSS section corners; the Duluth News Tribune 1906 original names the Martin Millet farm in Lexington Twp. Farm not yet placed on a plat.

1898 Le Sueur plat (Ancestry image 31617_072135-00499): a Reinhardt family tract ('S. Reinhardt 83'), N half sec 18 T111N R25W (Sharon Twp), ~44.424,-93.884, ~7 mi S of Henderson; whether it is the 1858 Reinhart clearing is unproven.

1860 census puts a Sebastian Reinhardt household in Sharon Twp, tying the 1898 'S. Reinhardt 83' tract (N sec 18 T111N R25W, 44.424,-93.884) to the 1858 family; that clearing is the likely murder site, the Millet farm the 1906 find site.
Reinhardt household present in Sharon Twp 1860, absent 1870 (no 1857 index hit); an heir holds the tract on the 1898 plate. Inconclusive for the 1858 hanging tale.
1900 census, Sharon Twp: Sebastian Reinhardt, b. 1814, aged 85, wife Anna, son John b. 1869, so the 'S. Reinhardt' of the 1898 plate is Sebastian Sr., alive 42 years after the 1858 'hanging'.
set.t: Part found 1906 ($140); the balance of the German's ~$600, if it exists, is unplaced. Private farm. Caution: Sebastian Reinhardt (b. 1814) was still alive in Sharon Twp in 1900, 42 years after the 1858 'hanging', so the lynched man was someone else or the tale is garbled; the 1906 find is the only hard fact.

src: 1900 US census, Sharon Twp, Le Sueur Co, MN (Sebastian Reinhardt)
